newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Australia to maintain higher gold output.
newsitem.headline: Australia to maintain higher gold output.

text.p: Australia has raised its annual gold production to 270 tonnes or eight million ounces a year with reserves available to support that level for a further eight years though intensive exploration, speakers told the ABN-AMRO world gold conference on Tuesday.
Drilling has taken place not only in areas where gold was already known to exist but also in "green field sites"
David Walker research director at ABN-AMRO Australia noted the major Australia finds since 1989 were in new gold mining areas.

The country's seven major producers account for about 50 percent of a total exploration budget of A$500 million but the junior companies which produce about 10 percent of Australia's gold output accounted for 20 percent of the exploration spend.
"Increased production requires increased exploration to keep up," he said.
Three of the new promising areas came from different exploration philosophies, Walker said.
The Gawler development was originated by state government inspired drilling programmes and did not attract any interest from the leading Australian miners.
Ashburton was close to established iron ore mines but attracted little drilling for gold due to "formidable geology," Walker said.
But the Sipa mining company which unearthed the deposits now had reserves containing two million ounces and around $4 million had been raised for exploration in the area.
Lachlan in New South Wales was in a well explored area near copper deposits. New geological techniques in porphyry rock area had turned up a 10 million ounce gold prospect, he said.
Eduard Eshuys a director of resources at the Great Central Mines-Centaur mining group told delegates, "If you want to find gold, look where it has been found,"
The group was concentrating its searches in Western Australia near its established mines where its drilling programme had been increased from 62,000 metres to 990,000 metres between 1989 and 1996.
"You can only do that if you can show results".
The Great Centaur group was spending $75 million on exploration last year, he said.
"Intensive drilling turns resources into reserves," Eshuys said. Drilling was critical in Western Australia due to its desert terrain which produced wide variations in deposit depth.
The company's Jundee deposit was in a known mining area and only one metre under the desert as were some points on the Yandal belt which also hosted its Bronze Wing deposit.
"We are looking for a third major discovery on the Yandal belt Eshuys told delegates.
Bronze Wing produced 270,000 ounces to be the fifth largest Australian gold mine and Jundee was 236,000 ounces, the seventh largest.
Their reserves were 3.6 million and 2.7 million ounces respectively.
Centaur concentrated its exploration about 20 kilometres north of Kalgoorlie where 45 million ounces of gold had been mined over the past 100 years leaving about 20 million ounces in the ground.
The areas was assumed to be fully drilled but Eshuys noted that 30 percent of the drill holes were to a depth of only 20 metres whereas the average deposit was located at 30 metres of more.
The 1.7 million ounces of gold contained in the quarter's deposit was located at depth of 35 metres, he said.
Centaur was now looking for gold in granite rock "Which could open up new opportunities for Western Australia."
Australian average production costs were A$354 an ounce against gold prices last year of A$450 and, through forward selling, average receipts of A$587 an ounce.
"The Australian gold mining industry is in a very healthy position," Eshuys said.
